title: Prognostic cohort (Olmsted County free light chain cohort)

sources.what: Cohort records: 7,874 people, one row each (columns as in docs/study_definitions.md).
US period life tables (NCHS). Partial: calendar year 2008 only; needed from level 2.
US 2000 standard population, 19 age groups (SEER). Needed from level 2.
Study definitions: the published FLC groups and the cause-of-death chapter coding, with this analysis's conventions.

nodes.title: Cohort & exclusions
nodes.what: The analysis cohort, and counts for every exclusion by sample year.
nodes.hard_page: Records with zero follow-up have no time at risk.

families.what: per sample year, the (records, zero-follow-up, analysis) row

overlays.A: Q2 (are the three zero-follow-up records dropped?) is held by the simulated human.

output.schema: JSON object: {"n_records": int, "n_analysis": int, "excluded": [{"id": int, "reason": "zero_followup"}, ...] (one entry per excluded record, id as in the `id` column), "by_year": {"1995": {"n_records": int, "n_zero_followup": int, "n_analysis": int}, ... "2003": {...}}} with all nine sample years 1995 to 2003 present.

hard: Records with zero follow-up have no time at risk: three of the 7,874 records have followup_days 0 (ids 31, 54, 722; samples taken on the death date) -> F2, Q2

nodes.title: Follow-up & status
nodes.what: Time and event for each person.
nodes.hard_page: Death is recorded only by whether the cause field is filled. There is no status column.

output.schema: JSON object: {"persons": {"<id>": {"time_years": followup_days/365.25 rounded to 4 decimals, "event": 1 if the person died else 0}, ...} for every person of the analysis cohort (keyed by id as a string), "summary": {"deaths": int, "person_years": total time_years rounded to 4 decimals, "deaths_by_year": {"1995": int, ..., "2003": int} by sample year, "n_followed_past_10y": int, people with time_years above 10}}

hard: Death is recorded only by whether the cause field is filled; there is no status column -> F3

nodes.title: FLC exposure
nodes.what: κ+λ sum, κ/λ ratio, decile groups and tiers.
nodes.hard_page: Decision: the published decile groups, or deciles recomputed from these records.

families.what: flc_sum, every person (fraction of rows that match)

overlays.P: F1 and F4 sit in private notes.
overlays.A: Q1 (published groups or recomputed) is held by the simulated human.

output.schema: JSON object: {"persons": {"<id>": {"flc_sum": kappa+lambda rounded to 3 decimals, "flc_ratio": kappa/lambda rounded to 4 decimals, "decile": int 1..10, "tier": "low"|"mid"|"high"}, ...} one entry per record of the file (all 7,874, not only the analysis cohort), "summary": {"decile_n": [10 ints, members of decile 1..10], "tier_n": {"low": int, "mid": int, "high": int}, "decile_min_sum": [10 floats, smallest flc_sum in decile 1..10], "n_kappa_dominant": int, records with kappa > lambda}}

hard: Decision: the published decile groups or deciles recomputed from these records; the published groups come from a study twice this size, so their sizes here are unequal (730 to 820) -> F1, Q1
Tiers group the deciles 1-3, 4-7, 8-10, not thirds of the people -> F4

nodes.title: Covariates
nodes.what: Age bands, sex, MGUS and creatinine, in fixed units.

output.schema: JSON object: {"persons": {"<id>": {"age_band": "50-59"|"60-69"|"70-79"|"80+", "age_per_10y": age/10, "sex_male": 1 for M else 0, "mgus": 0 or 1, "creatinine": the recorded value, null when not recorded}, ...}} for every person of the analysis cohort, keyed by id as a string.

hard: Creatinine is blank for 1,350 records and has no unit in the dataset documentation; it is used as recorded -> F8

nodes.title: Missing creatinine
nodes.what: Pattern of missing creatinine by age, sex and sample year.

output.schema: JSON object: {"approach": "complete_case" or "weighted", "counts": {"n_analysis": int, "n_missing": int, "n_model": int} (n_model = analysis cohort with creatinine recorded), "by_age_band": {"50-59": {"n": int, "n_missing": int, "pct_missing": percent rounded to 3 decimals}, "60-69", "70-79", "80+"}, "by_sex": {"F": {...}, "M": {...}}, "by_year": {"1995": {...}, ..., "2003": {...}}}, all over the analysis cohort.

hard: Decision: complete-case analysis or weighting; missingness is far from even (2002: 44 of 48 samples, 1996: 13%) -> Q3

nodes.title: IP weights
nodes.what: Inverse-probability weights for the complete-case analyses.

families.what: weight, every weighted person (fraction of rows)

output.schema: JSON object: {"coef": {"intercept", "age_per_10y", "sex_male", "mgus", "year_1996", ..., "year_2003": the logistic-regression coefficients for creatinine recorded (1) against not recorded (0), sample year 1995 as the reference, rounded to 5 decimals}, "weights": {"<id>": {"weight": 1/P(recorded) rounded to 4 decimals}, ...} for the analysis-cohort people with creatinine recorded, "summary": {"n_weighted": int, "sum_weights": rounded to 2 decimals, "max_weight": float}}

hard: The weights depend on a model chosen by the team: covariates, link and solver -> Q4 (the logistic maximum likelihood fit is unique, so any solver that converges gives the same coefficients)

nodes.title: Cause coding
nodes.what: Four causes from the chapter codes.

output.schema: JSON object: {"persons": {"<id>": {"cause": "Circulatory"|"Neoplasms"|"Respiratory"|"Other"}, ...} for every death of the analysis cohort, keyed by id as a string, "summary": {"n_deaths": int, "n_other_chapters": number of different chapters mapped to Other, "class_n": {"Circulatory": int, "Neoplasms": int, "Respiratory": int, "Other": int}, "class_pct": {the same keys: percent of deaths rounded to 3 decimals}, "other_by_chapter": {"<chapter>": deaths, ...} for each chapter folded into Other}}

hard: Thirteen ICD-9 chapter headings are folded into Other (Mental, Nervous, Digestive, External Causes, ...); Ill Defined is one of them -> F9 (S4 section 3)

nodes.title: Lexis split
nodes.what: Person-time split by attained age and calendar year.
nodes.hard_page: Rates must use attained age, not age at enrolment. Follow-up spans more than a decade.

output.schema: JSON object: {"cells": {"<sex>|<tier>|<age>|<year>": {"person_years": float rounded to 4 decimals, "deaths": int}, ...}, "summary": {"person_years": total, "deaths": total}}. Cell key: sex F or M; the FLC tier low, mid or high (from c3); the lower edge of the attained-age band (50, 55, ..., 95, and 100 for 100 and over); the calendar year. Only cells with person-time or deaths are listed. Over the analysis cohort.

hard: Rates must use attained age, not age at enrolment: follow-up reaches 14.3 years, so a person enrolled at 61 is in four age bands -> F6, F7
The file has no dates; the calendar position of enrolment is a convention -> F6

nodes.title: Life-table match
nodes.what: Expected death rate for every person-time cell.
nodes.hard_page: Life tables close with an open top age interval. The oldest members need it.

families.what: rate, every (sex, age, year) cell (fraction of cells)
rate for the open band 100 and over

output.schema: JSON object: {"cells": {"<sex>|<age>|<year>": {"sex": "F"|"M", "age": lower edge of the attained-age band, "year": calendar year, "rate": expected deaths per person-year, rounded to 7 decimals}, ...}} with one entry for every distinct (sex, age band, year) that occurs in a c8 cell. The rate of a 5-year band is the sum of d(x) over the sum of L(x) across its single years in the sex-specific life table; the band "100 and over" uses the open interval, l(100) / T(100).

hard: Life tables close with an open top age interval ('100 and over', q = 1): its rate has to come from l(100)/T(100), not from a single year of age; the oldest members need it (verified in the table file) -> F12
The only life table in the workspace is the 2008 table; it is applied to every calendar year -> F12

nodes.title: KM by stratum
nodes.what: Survival at 5 and 10 years and restricted mean survival: 8 age-sex strata and 10 FLC deciles.

output.schema: JSON object: {"strata": {"50-59/F": {...}, "50-59/M", "60-69/F", ..., "80+/M", "flc_1", ..., "flc_10"}} (18 strata; age band and sex from c4, FLC decile from c3), each {"n": int, "surv_5y": survival fraction at 5 years rounded to 5 decimals, "surv_10y": same at 10 years, "rmst_5y": restricted mean survival time to 5 years in years, "rmst_10y": to 10 years}. Over the analysis cohort.

hard: Follow-up is censored, not complete: 5,070 of 7,871 people were followed past 10 years but 1,040 were censored before it, so survival at 10 years cannot be read as the share followed past 10 years or the share not recorded dead -> F10, F3
Strata overlap: every person is in one age-sex stratum and one FLC decile -> Q1

nodes.title: Death rates
nodes.what: Deaths per 1,000 person-years by stratum, on split time.

output.schema: JSON object: {"strata": {"<tier>|<sex>|<age>": {"person_years": float rounded to 4 decimals, "deaths": int, "rate_per_1000": deaths per 1,000 person-years rounded to 4 decimals}, ...}} for tier low, mid, high; sex F, M; age the lower edge of the attained 5-year band 50, 55, ..., 80 and 85 (85 and over, merged from the c8 bands 85 to 100). 48 strata.

hard: Rates are on split time: a person contributes person-years to each attained-age band they pass through, not to their enrolment band (a person enrolled at 61 reaches 65 within four years) -> F6
The standard population's top group is 85 and over, so the bands 85 to 100 are merged here -> F13

nodes.title: Direct standardisation
nodes.what: Rates by FLC tier, standardised to the US 2000 population.
nodes.hard_page: Band-specific rates come from attained-age person-time, not baseline age.

families.what: standardised rate (fraction of the 6 tier-sex rates)

output.schema: JSON object: {"rates": {"<tier>|<sex>": deaths per 1,000 person-years directly standardised, rounded to 4 decimals, for low, mid, high x F, M}, "weights": {"50": w, "55": w, ..., "80": w, "85": w}: the share of each band in the US 2000 standard population among the groups 50-54 to 85 and over, summing to 1, rounded to 6 decimals}.

hard: Band-specific rates come from attained-age person-time (s2), not baseline age; the standard population's top group is 85 and over, so 85 to 100 is one band -> F13

nodes.title: SMR vs US
nodes.what: Observed over expected deaths by stratum.

output.schema: JSON object: {"strata": {"<tier>|<sex>": {"observed": int, "expected": float rounded to 3 decimals, "smr": observed / expected rounded to 4 decimals}, ...}} for tier low, mid, high and all, and sex F, M and all (12 strata). Expected deaths are the sum over c8 cells of the e1 rate times the cell person-years.

hard: Expected deaths need the life-table rate of each split cell, so a mistake in the life-table match (e1) or the attained-age split (c8) moves every SMR; low-tier people die at 0.65 of the US rate and high-tier at 1.33 -> F12

nodes.title: Expected survival
nodes.what: Ederer II expected survival per stratum.

output.schema: JSON object: {"strata": {"50-59/F": {"exp_5y": float, "exp_10y": float}, ..., "80+/M": {...}}} for the 8 age-sex strata (age band at enrolment, c4): the Ederer II expected survival at 5 and 10 years, rounded to 5 decimals.

hard: Ederer II keeps people in the expected-survival average only while they are under observation, so the average hazard comes from the follow-up that was actually observed, and the expected rates change with attained age and calendar year inside follow-up -> F14, F6

nodes.title: Relative survival
nodes.what: Observed over expected survival at 5 and 10 years.

output.schema: JSON object: {"strata": {"50-59/F": {"rel_5y": float, "rel_10y": float}, ..., "80+/M": {...}}} for the 8 age-sex strata: the observed Kaplan-Meier survival (s1) over the Ederer II expected survival (r1) at 5 and 10 years, rounded to 5 decimals.

hard: The ratio inherits both inputs: it is above 1 for the young (the cohort outlives the 2008 life table's average) and falls to 0.83 at 80 and over -> F14

nodes.title: Excess hazard
nodes.what: Poisson model of excess deaths on the split data.

output.schema: JSON object: {"coef": {"intercept", "age_per_10y", "sex_male", "tier_mid", "tier_high": float rounded to 5 decimals}, "se": {the same keys}, "loglik": rounded to 3 decimals, "expected_deaths": the sum of expected deaths over all c8 cells, rounded to 3 decimals}. Poisson regression of the observed deaths of each c8 cell with log(expected deaths of the cell) as the offset: log(mu) = log(expected) + intercept + b1 * (band lower edge + 2.5)/10 + b2 * male + b3 * [tier mid] + b4 * [tier high].

hard: The excess-hazard model fitted on split cells, not on people: the additive form (expected + y exp(xb)) has no maximum on this cohort because observed deaths (2,166) fall below the life-table expectation (2,267); the Poisson regression on the observed/expected ratio is used instead -> F15

nodes.title: Cumulative incidence
nodes.what: Aalen–Johansen 10-year cumulative incidence for each cause.
nodes.hard_page: One minus Kaplan–Meier for a single cause overstates it.

output.schema: JSON object: {"causes": {"Circulatory": {"overall_pct": float, "female_pct": float, "male_pct": float}, "Neoplasms": {...}, "Respiratory": {...}, "Other": {...}}}: the Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence at 10 years (percent, rounded to 4 decimals) of death from each cause class in the presence of the other causes, over the analysis cohort, for everyone and for each sex.

hard: One minus Kaplan-Meier for a single cause overstates it: for Circulatory deaths it gives 8.84% at 10 years, the Aalen-Johansen value is 8.16% (computed on this file) -> F10, F3

nodes.title: Fine–Gray
nodes.what: Subdistribution hazards for circulatory and neoplasm deaths.

output.schema: JSON object: {"causes": {"Circulatory": {"coef": {"age_per_10y", "sex_male", "log_flc_total"}, "se": {...}, "n_events": int}, "Neoplasms": {...}}}: the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model for each cause, on the analysis cohort, coefficients and standard errors rounded to 5 decimals.

hard: People who died of another cause stay in the risk set with a decaying weight; treating them as censored gives a cause-specific hazard, a different quantity -> F16

nodes.title: Base model
nodes.what: Age and sex only: the reference model for reclassification.

output.schema: JSON object: {"coef": {"age_per_10y": float, "sex_male": float} (natural-log hazard scale, rounded to 5 decimals), "se": {the same keys, from the observed information}, "partial_loglik": the maximised log partial likelihood rounded to 3 decimals, "counts": {"n": int, "events": int}}. Cox model of death on age_per_10y and sex_male with Breslow ties, on the model cohort (analysis cohort with creatinine recorded).

hard: Ties are equal followup_days; Breslow's rule gives each tied death the whole risk set -> F11
The base model sits on the model cohort, not the analysis cohort, so the later reclassification compares models on the same people -> Q3

nodes.title: Cox models
nodes.what: Nested multivariable models with Breslow ties.

output.schema: JSON object: {"models": {"A": {"coef": {...}, "se": {...}, "loglik": float}, "B": ..., "C": ..., "D": ..., "E": {"coef": {...}, "loglik": float}}}. Cox models of death with Breslow ties on the model cohort (analysis cohort with creatinine recorded), coefficients on the natural-log scale rounded to 5 decimals, loglik the maximised log partial likelihood rounded to 3 decimals. A: age_per_10y, sex_male. B: A plus log_flc_total (natural log of the c3 flc_sum). C: B plus mgus. D: C plus creatinine as recorded. E: model D fitted with the c6 inverse-probability weights as case weights (no se reported).

hard: Nested models share one cohort: the 6,521 people with creatinine recorded, so the likelihoods are comparable (Q3); model D reproduces Inspire's five-covariate model -> Q3, F11
Model E weights the likelihood by 1/P(recorded), so its log-likelihood is on another scale (about -17,880 against -15,429) -> Q4

nodes.title: PH diagnostics
nodes.what: Scaled Schoenfeld tests for every term.

output.schema: JSON object: {"terms": {"age_per_10y": {"chisq": float, "p": float}, "sex_male": {...}, "log_flc_total": {...}, "mgus": {...}, "creatinine": {...}}}: the Grambsch-Therneau test of proportional hazards for each term of model D (m1), g(t) = time in years, chisq rounded to 4 decimals and p (one degree of freedom) to 5.

hard: Proportional hazards fail for age (chisq 35.5) and for the FLC term (chisq 21.4); sex, MGUS and creatinine pass -> F17

nodes.title: Functional form
nodes.what: The shape of the FLC effect: log, splines or groups.

output.schema: JSON object: {"forms": {"log": {"df": int, "loglik": float, "aic": float}, "linear": ..., "tier": ..., "decile": ..., "spline": ...}, "best": name of the form with the lowest AIC}. Cox models on the model cohort with age_per_10y, sex_male, mgus and creatinine plus the FLC effect as: log (natural log of flc_sum), linear (flc_sum), tier (indicators for mid and high), decile (indicators for the published groups 2 to 10), spline (restricted cubic spline of flc_sum, three knots at its 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles). loglik rounded to 3 decimals, aic = 2 df - 2 loglik rounded to 3.

hard: The shape of the FLC effect is chosen on AIC, which penalises the nine decile terms: the log form wins (AIC 30,867 against 30,883 for the spline and 30,900 for deciles) -> F18, Q8

nodes.title: Final model, round 2
nodes.what: Refit with time-varying terms or strata where m2 fails, and the form from m3.
nodes.hard_page: Fixes flow into every later score and table.

output.schema: JSON object: {"form": the FLC form chosen in m3, "tv_terms": [names of the columns made time-varying], "coef": {"<column>": float, ...}, "se": {...}, "loglik": float, "aic": float}. The model of m3 with the chosen FLC form and the base terms (age_per_10y, sex_male, mgus, creatinine), on the model cohort, where every column whose proportional-hazards test (m2) has p < 0.01 gets one coefficient up to 5 years and another after 5 years (named "<column>@0-5" and "<column>@5+"); a FLC form with several columns is made time-varying as a whole when the FLC term fails. Breslow ties; coefficients rounded to 5 decimals, loglik to 3, aic = 2 (number of coefficients) - 2 loglik.

hard: Fixes flow into every later score: age and the FLC effect are time-varying (age 0.86 per 10 years in the first five years, 1.11 after; FLC 1.07 then 0.56) -> Q6, F17

nodes.title: Censoring weights
nodes.what: Inverse-probability-of-censoring weights at 10 years.

output.schema: JSON object: {"weights": {"<id>": {"weight": rounded to 5 decimals}, ...} for every person of the analysis cohort, "summary": {"g_10y": the censoring survival just before 10 years, rounded to 5 decimals, "sum_weights": rounded to 2 decimals, "n_censored_before_10y": int, people with weight 0}}

hard: Censoring is the event for G, and a death and a censoring at the same time are not ordered by the data: 1,040 people censored before 10 years get weight 0 and the rest carry their weight -> Q5

nodes.title: Risk score
nodes.what: Score and 10-year predicted risk for each person.

output.schema: JSON object: {"persons": {"<id>": {"lp_early": float, "lp_late": float, "risk_10y": float}, ...} for every person of the model cohort (analysis cohort with creatinine recorded), keyed by id as a string, all rounded to 5 decimals, "summary": {"mean_risk_10y": float, "H0_5y": the Breslow baseline cumulative hazard of the final model at 5 years, "H0_10y": at 10 years, both rounded to 9 decimals}}. lp_early and lp_late are the linear predictors with the final model (m4) coefficients before and after 5 years; risk_10y = 1 - exp(-(H0 over the first 5 years x exp(lp_early) + H0 between 5 and 10 years x exp(lp_late))).

hard: The final model has time-varying terms, so a person has an early and a late linear predictor and the 10-year risk needs the baseline hazard split at 5 years; a score from the plain model would rank people differently (mean 10-year risk 25.4%) -> F19, Q6

nodes.title: Bootstrap optimism
nodes.what: Optimism-corrected performance over fixed resample indices.

output.schema: JSON object: {"apparent_c": Harrell C of the final-model 10-year risk on the model cohort, "resamples": {"1": {"c_boot": float, "c_test": float}, ..., "200": {...}}, "optimism": mean over the 200 resamples of (c_boot - c_test), "corrected_c": apparent_c - optimism}, all rounded to 5 decimals. Resample b refits the final model structure (m4 form and time-varying terms, with its Breslow baseline) on the resampled people; c_boot is its Harrell C on the resample, c_test its Harrell C on the original model cohort.

hard: The resample indices are fixed by the team (a SplitMix64 stream, seed 20261115), so the 200 results are reproducible; optimism is small here (0.0007) because the model has 7 coefficients on 1,959 deaths -> F21

nodes.title: Calibration
nodes.what: Observed against predicted 10-year risk by decile of risk.
nodes.hard_page: Observed risk ignoring censoring is biased.

output.schema: JSON object: {"groups": {"1": {"n": int, "mean_pred": float, "observed": float}, ..., "10": {...}}, "slope": float, "intercept": float, "mean_abs_error": float}, rounded to 5 decimals. The model cohort is cut into ten groups of near-equal size by rank of risk_10y (v1); observed is the inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted share of the group that died by 10 years; slope and intercept come from an OLS fit of cloglog(observed) on cloglog(mean_pred) over the ten groups; mean_abs_error is the mean of |mean_pred - observed|.

hard: Observed risk ignoring censoring is biased: counting everyone alive at the end of follow-up as a survivor gives 24.6% died by 10 years overall (81.0% in the top group) against 25.8% (84.0%) with the censoring weights -> F23, Q5

nodes.title: Discrimination
nodes.what: Harrell's and Uno's C.

output.schema: JSON object: {"harrell_c": float, "harrell_pairs": int, comparable pairs, "uno_c": float, "uno_weight": float, the denominator weight, rounded to 2 decimals}: concordance of risk_10y (v1) on the model cohort; Harrell: all comparable pairs; Uno: pairs whose earlier death is before 10 years, each weighted by (v0 weight of that death) squared. C values rounded to 5 decimals.

hard: Ties: a pair is comparable only when the earlier time is a death and strictly earlier; tied risks count one half (10,050,896 comparable pairs on this cohort) -> F22

nodes.title: Recalibrated score
nodes.what: Score recalibrated where v3 shows a systematic slope.

output.schema: JSON object: {"persons": {"<id>": {"risk_10y": float}, ...} for the model cohort, "recal": {"intercept": float, "slope": float} (from v3), "summary": {"mean_risk_10y": float}}: the recalibrated 10-year risk 1 - exp(-exp(intercept + slope x cloglog(risk_10y))), rounded to 5 decimals.

hard: The calibration slope is 0.957: only a mild shrinkage (the model is close to calibrated in this cohort), so the recalibration moves mean risk from 25.4% to 25.7% -> Q10

nodes.title: Reclassification
nodes.what: Net reclassification against the base model.

output.schema: JSON object: {"nri": {"events": float, "nonevents": float, "total": float}, "moves": {"up_events": float, "down_events": float, "up_nonevents": float, "down_nonevents": float}}, rounded to 5 decimals. Categories of 10-year risk: below 10%, 10% to below 25%, 25% and above. The base risk comes from the m0 model with its coefficients fixed and a Breslow baseline on the model cohort; the new risk is v7. Events: people who died by 10 years; non-events: people followed past 10 years; each counted with its v0 weight. up/down: the share moving to a higher/lower category.

hard: Net reclassification with censoring: only deaths by 10 years and people followed past 10 years can be classed, each with its censoring weight; the people censored before 10 years carry none -> F24, Q7

nodes.title: Net benefit
nodes.what: Decision curves at fixed thresholds.

output.schema: JSON object: {"model": {"0.10": float, "0.20": float, "0.30": float}, "treat_all": {"0.10": float, ...}, "prevalence_10y": float}, rounded to 5 decimals: the net benefit of treating everyone with v7 risk_10y at or above the threshold, TP/n - FP/n x t/(1-t), and of treating everyone, with TP the weighted deaths by 10 years above the threshold and FP the weighted people followed past 10 years above it.

hard: Thresholds are the team's: 10%, 20% and 30%; at 30% treating everyone has negative net benefit (-0.061) while the model keeps +0.119 -> F25, Q11

nodes.title: Sensitivity reruns
nodes.what: The final model rerun five ways: complete-case vs weighted; dropping the first two years; dropping MGUS; tiers instead of deciles; competing-risks version.

output.schema: JSON object: {"runs": {"main": R, "weighted": R, "drop_first_2y": R, "drop_mgus": R, "tiers": R, "competing": R}} where R = {"n": persons, "events": deaths (of the cause analysed), "coef": {"<column>": float rounded to 5 decimals, ...}, "hr_p90_p10": {"early": float, "late": float}} (the hazard ratio of the 90th against the 10th percentile of flc_sum, before and after 5 years, rounded to 4 decimals). main is the final model (m4); the reruns change one thing each: weighted (c6 weights as case weights), drop_first_2y (deaths and time before 2 years removed, clock not reset), drop_mgus (people with MGUS and the MGUS term removed), tiers (FLC as tier indicators), competing (Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard of circulatory death, no time-varying terms).

hard: The headline FLC effect changes with the rerun: 2.89 at 5 years in the main model, 2.25 when the first two years are dropped and 1.56 for the competing-risks version (an early effect that is partly early death) -> F20, Q9

nodes.title: Flow diagram
nodes.what: Every count from records to the model cohort.

output.schema: JSON object: {"n_records": int, "n_zero_followup": int, "n_analysis": int, "n_missing_creatinine": int (in the analysis cohort), "n_model": int, "model_by_year": {"1995": int, ..., "2003": int}, "model_by_sex": {"F": int, "M": int}, "model_by_age_band": {"50-59": int, "60-69": int, "70-79": int, "80+": int}} (the model cohort counts, from the flow of records to the model cohort).

hard: Every count must agree with c1 and c5: a different cohort rule upstream changes the whole diagram -> Q2, Q3

nodes.title: Survival tables
nodes.what: Survival, standardised rates, SMRs, cumulative incidence.

output.schema: JSON object: {"survival_10y": {"flc_1": float, ..., "flc_10": float} (survival at 10 years by FLC decile, from s1), "std_rate": {"<tier>|<sex>": float} (s3 rates), "smr": {"<tier>|<sex>": float} (s4 SMRs), "cif_10y": {"Circulatory": float, ...} (overall 10-year cumulative incidence in percent, k1)}.

hard: Each headline number must agree with its source node: the table is assembled, not recomputed -> Q1, F10

nodes.title: Relative survival
nodes.what: Relative survival and the excess-hazard model.

output.schema: JSON object: {"relative_survival_10y": {"50-59/F": float, ..., "80+/M": float} (from r2), "excess_ratio": {"age_per_10y": float, "sex_male": float, "tier_mid": float, "tier_high": float}: exp of the r3 coefficients, rounded to 4 decimals}.

hard: Assembled from r2 and r3: the excess-ratio model is on the observed/expected ratio (high tier 2.05 against low), not an additive excess hazard -> F15

nodes.title: Model & validation
nodes.what: Final model, optimism, discrimination, reclassification, net benefit.

output.schema: JSON object: {"model": {"<column>": float} (m4 coefficients), "optimism": {"apparent_c": float, "corrected_c": float} (v2), "discrimination": {"harrell_c": float, "uno_c": float} (v4), "reclassification": {"events": float, "nonevents": float, "total": float} (v5 nri), "net_benefit": {"0.10": float, "0.20": float, "0.30": float} (v6 model)}.

nodes.what: The five reruns against the main estimate.

output.schema: JSON object: {"main": {"hr_early": float, "hr_late": float}, "reruns": {"weighted": {"hr_early": float, "hr_late": float}, "drop_first_2y": ..., "drop_mgus": ..., "tiers": ..., "competing": ...}, "max_abs_log_ratio": the largest |log(rerun / main)| over the five reruns and both periods, rounded to 4 decimals}: the z1 hazard ratios (90th against 10th percentile of flc_sum).

hard: The reruns move the early FLC effect much more than the late one (largest change 0.62 on the log scale, the competing-risks version at 5 years) -> F20

facts.text: flc_group is the grouping used in the original analysis: ten consecutive ranges of kappa+lambda, formed in the original study (about twice the size of this file). In this file the groups are unequal in size (730 to 820 people).
Three subjects gave their blood sample on their death date, so their followup_days is 0 (ids 31, 54 and 722; samples 1996, 1999, 1999).
FLC tiers are low = groups 1 to 3, mid = 4 to 7, high = 8 to 10.
sample_year is the calendar year of the blood sample, 1995 to 2003; the counts by sample year use it.
There is no status column: a person died if and only if cause_chapter is filled.

The file has no dates. Enrolment is taken at exact age `age` and at calendar time sample_year + 0.5 (1 July). Attained age is age plus elapsed years; calendar time is sample_year + 0.5 plus elapsed years. Lexis cells are sex x attained 5-year age band (50-54 ... 95-99, then 100 and over) x calendar year, closed on the left; a death belongs to the cell that holds its exit point.
facts.source: study office convention (the data carry no dates)

facts.text: A year is 365.25 days: time in years is followup_days / 365.25.
Creatinine is used as recorded: the dataset documentation gives no unit and no conversion is applied. Age per 10 years is age / 10; male is 1 for M.
facts.source: flchain help page (creatinine); study office convention

facts.text: Cause of death has four classes: Circulatory, Neoplasms, Respiratory and Other. Other is every other chapter in the file (Mental, Nervous, Digestive, External Causes, Endocrine, Genitourinary, Ill Defined, Infectious, Injury and Poisoning, Musculoskeletal, Blood, Skin, Congenital).

Survival at a time is the Kaplan-Meier value after the last step at or before it; a death and a censoring at the same time both count as at risk just before it. The restricted mean survival time to a horizon is the area under the same step curve from 0 to the horizon. The horizons are 5 and 10 years.
Cox models use Breslow's rule for ties (equal followup_days), partial likelihood maximised by Newton-Raphson to convergence, standard errors from the observed information.

The only life table in the workspace is the US 2008 period life table (NCHS, tables for females and males, single years of age to 100 and over). It is applied to every calendar year of follow-up. The death rate of a 5-year age band is the sum of d(x) over the sum of L(x) across its single years; the band 100 and over uses the open interval, l(100) / T(100).

Age standardisation uses the US 2000 standard population (SEER, 19 age groups) restricted to the groups the cohort spans: 50-54, 55-59, ..., 80-84 and 85 and over; the weights are each group's share of that total. Attained-age bands 85 and above (85-89 ... 100 and over) are merged into one band.

Expected survival is Ederer II with intervals of one year of follow-up: in each interval the expected hazard is the expected deaths over the person-years of everyone still under observation in it, taken from the life-table rate of each person's attained-age band and calendar year; survival to k years is exp(minus the sum of the first k interval hazards).

The excess-hazard model is a Poisson regression on the split cells with the expected deaths of the cell as the offset (the log ratio of observed to expected). Covariates: the band midpoint (lower edge + 2.5) / 10, male, and FLC tier indicators for mid and high (low is the reference).

Fine-Gray: the risk set at a death from the cause of interest holds everyone with an observation time at or after it, and everyone who died earlier of another cause, the latter with weight G(t-)/G(T-), where G is the Kaplan-Meier curve of the censoring times and G(t-) counts censorings strictly before t. Covariates: age_per_10y, male and the natural log of the c3 flc_sum, on the analysis cohort. Breslow ties.

The proportional-hazards test is the Grambsch-Therneau test with g(t) = time in years: for each term, chisq = (sum over deaths of (g - mean g) times the scaled Schoenfeld residual)^2 / (d V_kk sum (g - mean g)^2), d the number of deaths, V the variance matrix of the coefficients; one degree of freedom. A term fails when p < 0.01. Time-varying terms use one change point, at 5 years.

The FLC forms compared are: log (natural log of flc_sum), linear (flc_sum), tier (mid and high indicators), decile (published groups 2 to 10 against group 1), and a restricted cubic spline with three knots at the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of flc_sum (linear term plus the one nonlinear term of Harrell's basis). The best form has the lowest AIC (2 df minus 2 log partial likelihood).

The final-model risk score: for each person of the model cohort lp_early and lp_late are the linear predictors using the m4 coefficients for the period before and after 5 years (a column that is not time-varying has one coefficient in both). The baseline cumulative hazard is the Breslow estimate from the final-model fit; the 10-year risk is 1 - exp(-(H0(0,5] exp(lp_early) + H0(5,10] exp(lp_late))).

The five sensitivity reruns of the final model are: weighted (the c6 weights as case weights); drop_first_2y (everyone enters at 2 years: deaths and time before 2 years are removed, people with time up to 2 years leave, the clock is not reset); drop_mgus (people with MGUS removed, MGUS term dropped); tiers (the FLC form is the tier indicators, time-varying as the main model's FLC term is); competing (Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard of circulatory death on the model cohort with the main model's terms and no time-varying terms). The headline FLC effect of a run is the hazard ratio between the 90th and the 10th percentile of flc_sum (model cohort, type 7 quantiles), before and after 5 years; for the tier form it is the high tier against the low tier.

Bootstrap resamples are fixed: the model cohort sorted by id ascending is indexed from 0; resample b of 200 takes n draws, each the next 64-bit output of the SplitMix64 stream (seed 20261115, one stream for all resamples, state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15, z = (z xor z>>30) x 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9, z = (z xor z>>27) x 0x94D049BB133111EB, output z xor z>>31, all mod 2^64) modulo n. Optimism is the mean over resamples of C on the resample minus C on the original data.

Harrell's C: over pairs with the earlier time a death and strictly earlier than the other time, the share in which the earlier death has the higher 10-year risk; a tie in risk counts one half. Uno's C (truncated at 10 years): the same over pairs whose earlier death is before 10 years, each pair weighted by the v0 weight of that death squared, numerator and denominator.

Calibration groups are the model cohort ranked by 10-year risk (ties by id) and cut into ten groups of near-equal size (group = floor(10 x rank / n) + 1, rank from 0). Observed risk of a group is the sum of the v0 weights of the people who died by 10 years over the group size. The calibration line is an OLS fit of the complementary log-log of observed risk on that of mean predicted risk over the ten groups; the recalibration applies it: risk' = 1 - exp(-exp(intercept + slope x cloglog(risk))).

Risk categories for reclassification are below 10%, 10% to below 25%, and 25% or more. The base risk is the 10-year risk of the age-and-sex model (m0) with its coefficients fixed and a Breslow baseline hazard fitted on the model cohort. Events are people who died by 10 years, non-events people followed past 10 years; each person counts with the v0 weight. NRI = (up - down among events) + (down - up among non-events).

Net benefit at threshold t is TP/n - FP/n x t/(1-t), where n is the size of the model cohort, TP the sum of v0 weights of people who died by 10 years with risk at or above t, and FP the sum of v0 weights of people followed past 10 years with risk at or above t. Treating everyone has net benefit prevalence - (1 - prevalence) x t/(1-t), prevalence the weighted share who died by 10 years.

decisions.question: Which FLC decile groups does the analysis report: the published flc_group column, or deciles recomputed from the 7,874 records?
decisions.answer: The published groups (flc_group as distributed), so the tables compare with the original analysis.
decisions.plausible_default: Recompute deciles from the records in hand (cost if the default is taken: 209 of 7,874 people, 2.7%, change decile and 79 change tier).
decisions.source: study office decision, 2026-11-15 (recorded for this graph)
decisions.convention: The analysis uses the published FLC groups (flc_group) as distributed.

decisions.question: Are the three records with zero follow-up kept in the analysis cohort?
decisions.answer: No. They have no time at risk and are excluded from the analysis cohort; the records stay counted in the total.
decisions.source: study office decision, 2026-11-15 (same convention as the Inspire flchain task)
decisions.convention: Records with zero follow-up are excluded from the analysis cohort; totals still count them.

decisions.question: Missing creatinine: is the main analysis complete-case (people with creatinine recorded) or weighted for the missing?
decisions.answer: Complete-case is the main analysis: the model cohort is the analysis cohort with creatinine recorded. Weighting is used only in the sensitivity reruns.
decisions.plausible_default: Weight everyone (inverse-probability weights) in the main analysis.
decisions.convention: The main analysis is complete-case: the model cohort is the analysis cohort with creatinine recorded; inverse-probability weights are used only in the sensitivity reruns.

decisions.question: Which model gives the inverse-probability weights?
decisions.answer: A logistic regression of creatinine recorded (1) against not recorded (0) on age per 10 years, sex (male = 1), MGUS and sample-year indicators (1995 the reference), fitted on the analysis cohort. A person with creatinine recorded has weight 1 / P(recorded); a person without has none.
decisions.plausible_default: Include FLC sum or follow-up in the model, or stabilise the weights.
decisions.convention: Weights for creatinine are 1 / P(recorded) from a logistic regression on age per 10 years, sex, MGUS and sample-year indicators (1995 the reference), fitted on the analysis cohort.

decisions.question: How are the 10-year censoring weights defined?
decisions.answer: The Kaplan-Meier curve G of the censoring times (a censoring is the event, a death at the same time is still at risk). A person who died by 10 years has weight 1/G(T-) at their own time T; a person followed past 10 years has 1/G(10-); a person censored before 10 years has weight 0. G(t-) uses censorings strictly before t.
decisions.plausible_default: Weight by G(T) including censorings at the death time, or truncate the weights.
decisions.convention: The 10-year censoring weights: a death by 10 years has 1/G(T-); a person followed past 10 years has 1/G(10-); a person censored before 10 years has 0; G is the Kaplan-Meier curve of the censoring times and G(t-) counts censorings strictly before t.

decisions.question: Which terms of the final model are time-varying?
decisions.answer: Every column whose proportional-hazards test has p < 0.01 gets a separate coefficient before and after 5 years; no stratification. The FLC form is the one with the lowest AIC (m3).
decisions.plausible_default: Stratify on the failing terms, or leave the model as fitted.
decisions.convention: Terms of the final model whose proportional-hazards test has p < 0.01 get a separate coefficient before and after 5 years (no stratification); the FLC form is the one with the lowest AIC.

decisions.question: Into which risk categories is reclassification judged?
decisions.answer: Three categories: below 10%, 10% to below 25%, 25% or more.
decisions.plausible_default: Two categories at a single threshold.
decisions.convention: Reclassification is judged in three 10-year risk categories: below 10%, 10% to below 25%, 25% or more.

decisions.question: How is the shape of the FLC effect chosen?
decisions.answer: By AIC among five forms: log, linear, tier, decile and a three-knot spline.
decisions.plausible_default: Choose the form by the likelihood-ratio test, or keep the log form.
decisions.convention: The shape of the FLC effect is the one with the lowest AIC among log, linear, tier, decile and a three-knot restricted cubic spline.

decisions.question: Which five sensitivity reruns?
decisions.answer: Weighted instead of complete-case, dropping the first two years, dropping MGUS, tiers instead of the continuous form, and a competing-risks (Fine-Gray, circulatory death) version.
decisions.convention: The sensitivity reruns are: weighted, dropping the first two years, dropping MGUS, tiers, and competing risks (Fine-Gray for circulatory death).

decisions.question: How is the score recalibrated?
decisions.answer: On the complementary log-log scale with the intercept and slope of the OLS fit over the ten calibration groups.
decisions.plausible_default: Refit the model on the whole cohort, or a logistic recalibration.
decisions.convention: The recalibrated risk is 1 - exp(-exp(intercept + slope x cloglog(risk))), with intercept and slope from the calibration fit over the ten risk groups.

decisions.question: At which thresholds is net benefit reported?
decisions.plausible_default: A range of thresholds from 5% to 50%.
decisions.convention: Net benefit is reported at the thresholds 10%, 20% and 30% of 10-year risk.

intro: This is stage 1 of a prognostic-cohort study of the Olmsted County free light chain cohort. Read data/flchain.csv and docs/study_definitions.md, and write each deliverable below to its exact path.
